decisive_join: Test whether selected-survivor data create a structurally missing-outcome problem and whether exploration and shared-vendor evidence provide bounded remedies and risks.

findings.claim: Learning from selected survivors is selection-conditioned learning rather than neutral observation of the full applicant population.
limits: The magnitude and direction of bias depend on the historical policy, labels, and deployment.

findings.claim: An exploration budget is an empirically testable way to make some otherwise missing outcomes observable, but the studied design is not a universal policy or entitlement.
limits: Privacy, consent, role relevance, accommodations, and labor burdens require separate controls.

findings.claim: Shared-vendor screening creates empirically supported cross-employer monoculture risk, weakening the assumption that repeated applications always receive independent judgment.
limits: The finding is limited to the studied vendor ecosystem and recommendations, not every final employer decision.

findings.claim: Institutional resemblance can be reported as prediction when targets encode prior selection, ratings, sponsorship, and opportunity, but the full causal pathway remains deployment-specific.
limits: The exact target, proxies, label contamination, feedback response, and counterfactual outcomes remain open.

observations.notes: The label set is conditioned on prior opportunity allocation.
observations.subject: Historical hiring policy
observations.value: workplace outcomes are observed principally for selected candidates

observations.notes: The employer and vendor choose which outcomes count as success.
observations.subject: Selected employee labels

observations.notes: A consequential predictor can change the future population and outcomes on which it is evaluated.
observations.subject: Deployed prediction

observations.notes: One study demonstrates an empirical route to learning from candidates an exploitative policy would not select.
observations.subject: Exploration policy
observations.value: bounded uncertain candidates advanced under a contextual-bandit policy

observations.notes: Repeated all-position rejection recommendations exceeded an independence baseline in the studied ecosystem.
observations.subject: Shared screening vendor

observations.notes: The evidence does not establish that every employer uses the same system or follows every recommendation.
observations.subject: Universal employer market

selection_rule: Use formal and hiring-specific research to separate general mechanisms, one observed intervention, and one observed cross-employer vendor ecology.

prohibited_inferences: every rejected candidate would have succeeded
every shared vendor decision is identical
the exploration study mandates automatic advancement

title: Selective labels, performativity, exploration, and monoculture
